name: Bayonne
title: Bayonne Ship Gauging | UTM on the Adour for Bulkers & Coasters
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement at Bayonne and Tarnos on the Adour: bulk carriers, steel and fertiliser ships, coasters and tankers gauged alongside by UTM.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Ships at Bayonne and Tarnos
intro: Bayonne is a river port on the Adour, close to the Spanish border, with its working quays on both banks near the river mouth at Tarnos and Le Boucau. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships bring fertiliser, sulphur, steel, grain and timber. Superintendents call for gauging when a coaster or bulker is due a survey or needs steel readings before a docking nearby. Technicians travel from India to join the ship for the job, since nothing is based on this stretch of coast.

highlights.p: Ships berth on both banks close to the river mouth. Alongside gauging is practical once the ship is moored and the agent has arranged gate passes, with quay access varying by terminal.
Handysize bulk carriers and general cargo ships dominate. Fertiliser and sulphur are harsh on hold coatings, so hold frames and tank tops are a regular target for gauging.
Docking yards in the Basque Country and Cantabria are a short voyage away. A call at Bayonne is a sensible place for pre-docking readings before a ship heads there.

p: The Port of Bayonne lies on the Adour, a few kilometres from its mouth in the Bay of Biscay. The river enters the sea between two breakwaters south of Anglet, and the quays line the lower river on both banks at Tarnos in the Landes department and Bayonne in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques. The port has been run by the regional authority of Nouvelle-Aquitaine since the state transferred it, and it is separate from the large container ports on the Channel and Atlantic coasts. Its trade is bulk and general cargo, not boxes.

Handysize and smaller bulk carriers bring fertiliser, sulphur and other chemical cargoes, and take away grain and maize from the south-west farm belt. Steel products arrive for regional industry, timber and forest products pass in both directions, and a number of coasters carry mixed general cargo. Ship sizes are limited by the river's depth and the bar at the entrance, so the typical visitor is a handysize bulk carrier, a coaster or a small tanker of modest draught. There is no deep-sea anchorage inside the river, so waiting ships hold position offshore.

Weather and swell matter more at Bayonne than at most French ports. A strong Atlantic swell can break across the river bar, and pilots may delay entry or departure until conditions improve. A ship that expects to be gauged during a short call has to allow for those delays, and the team's arrival is booked only once the agent confirms the berth. In winter the Basque coast has frequent Atlantic depressions, and summer is calmer, so the quietest period for gauging is usually late spring through early autumn.

facilities.h: Where ships can be gauged at Bayonne
p: Gauging is done alongside at the working quays. Bulk quays at Tarnos and on the Bayonne side take fertiliser, sulphur and grain ships, and the team reaches the ship by quay gate with passes arranged by the agent. For a bulk carrier, the practical window is between discharge and loading when the holds are swept and the ship's crew can release hold spaces, hopper tanks and topside tanks for entry. Coasters and small tankers can be gauged during longer berth stays, for instance when waiting for cargo.

The river port is not a major repair centre, and its slipway and small repair quays suit local workboats, tugs and fishing craft rather than merchant ships. A merchant ship needing steel renewal usually goes to a yard in northern Spain, such as the Basque Country, or to a French yard further up the Atlantic coast, and the Bayonne call is useful for gauging before that voyage so the owner knows what to expect.
list: Tarnos bulk quays, for hold, hopper tank and hatch coaming gauging on fertiliser and sulphur carriers.
Bayonne river quays, for coasters, steel carriers and general cargo ships alongside.
Berths used by small tankers receiving fuel or chemical cargo, for ballast tank and deck gauging within terminal rules.
Grain quays during loading gaps, for hold structure checks on bulkers.
Slipway and small repair quays, for tugs and workboats rather than merchant ships.
Offshore waiting position beyond the bar, for launch-served work in calm weather only.

context.h: Port state control and regional rules at Bayonne
p: Ships calling at Bayonne fall under the Paris MoU, with inspections carried out by French ship safety centres of the maritime administration. Smaller, older ships carrying bulk chemicals and fertiliser fit a profile that the targeting system looks at closely. A recent gauging report on hold and tank structure helps the master show the condition of the steel if an inspector goes into the holds.

The EU Ship Recycling Regulation asks for an inventory of hazardous materials on ships calling at EU ports, EU ETS reaches voyages to Bayonne, and FuelEU Maritime applies to fuel burned on those calls. For the smaller ships that dominate here, the commercial driver is usually the charterer's or the financier's request for steel condition rather than regulation alone. Chemical cargoes such as sulphur and fertiliser can speed corrosion in hold plating and tank tops, which is why measuring them between voyages makes practical sense.

jobs.p: Typical work here is short, planned around a ship's berth stay and the quality of the weather. The superintendent shares the voyage and survey plan, the agent confirms the berth, and the team is booked once the pilot's arrival time looks firm. Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Bayonne often covers:
list: Hold frame, tank top and hopper tank gauging on a handysize bulker after discharging fertiliser or sulphur.
Hatch cover and coaming readings on a coaster after a season of grain and steel trading.
Ballast tank and cofferdam gauging on a small chemical tanker waiting for cargo at the berth.
Pre-docking steel estimate before a ship sails for a yard in northern Spain.
Owner's condition gauging on a general cargo ship before sale or a change of charter.

logistics: The team normally flies to Biarritz, which is the nearest airport and sits close to Bayonne, or to Bordeaux or Bilbao when schedules suit and then travels by road. The agent arranges gate passes for each quay. France is in the Schengen area, so every technician needs a Schengen visa from India before travel, and the visa decides the earliest start. We ask owners for the ship's expected berth as early as they can, because the river bar can delay arrivals.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged after fertiliser or sulphur is discharged?
faqs.a: Yes, once the holds are swept, washed where the cargo requires it, and the ship issues entry permits. Fertiliser and sulphur residues can hide wastage, so we ask for the hold to be cleaned as far as the crew can manage. Readings are recorded by frame and location for the next survey.

faqs.q: Does swell on the Adour bar affect your planning?
faqs.a: Yes. Swell can delay ship movements, which shifts the berth time and the team's arrival. We plan around the agent's confirmation and avoid committing the team until the ship is near the entrance. In heavy weather the job is rescheduled to the next call.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Bayonne?
faqs.a: Not for merchant ships of any size. The river port has a slipway and small repair quays used by workboats, tugs and fishing craft. Ships needing steel renewal normally sail to a yard in northern Spain or elsewhere in France, and gauging at Bayonne gives the owner readings before the yard is chosen.

faqs.q: Can gauging be done while the ship is loading grain?
faqs.a: Not in the holds being loaded. Ballast tanks, void spaces and deck structure can sometimes be gauged while loading if the ship releases them and the terminal permits entry. For hold structure we work in the gap between discharge and loading, which is when the holds are empty.

faqs.q: What documents does the ship need for tank and hold entry?
faqs.a: A gas-free certificate for tanks, an enclosed-space entry permit for each space, a rescue plan and ventilation in operation. The agent passes on any terminal rules, and the master confirms the sequence of spaces with the team before work begins.
